title: ClientMessage
description: Messages from the client to the service.

oneOf.description: Mandatory first message.

client_name.description: Client name, diagnostic only (truncated to 64 characters).

credential.description:
Channel credential: 32 bytes as 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits.
It stays free text in the schema so that a malformed credential
gives the same outcome (`unauthenticated`) as a missing or wrong one,
without distinguishing the reasons. Secret: never in logs or reports.

BaselineId.description: BaselineId: version 7 UUID, lowercase with hyphens.

Capability.description:
Authorizable action on a VM. Serialized names follow the MCP catalog
(ROADMAP 9); `vm.input` covers mouse and keyboard.

oneOf.description: List filtered by the grant.
Status.
Start.
Stop (ordinary or forced).
Reset: requires an explicit capability.
Screenshot.
Mouse and keyboard.
Checkpoint with the VM off: requires an explicit capability.
Restore with the VM off.
Authorized LightVM events and QEMU logs.

Firmware.description:
Guest firmware. Linux guests use UEFI with managed NVRAM state (ROADMAP 8,
ADR-0011); legacy Windows guests use SeaBIOS, which has no NVRAM
(ADR-0027). [`GuestOs::allowed_firmware`] says which applies.

oneOf.description: UEFI (OVMF) with per-VM NVRAM.
Legacy BIOS (SeaBIOS from the verified QEMU build), no NVRAM.

FixtureMarker.description: Marker expected by the fixture verifier.

oneOf.description: `LIGHTVM-FX1` on the data disk (after `fx.sh scrivi`).
No marker.

GuestOs.description:
Declared guest operating system. In the MVP the reference is Ubuntu LTS
x86_64 with the version and checksum pinned in F0 (ROADMAP 4). The
Windows variants (ADR-0027, ROADMAP R2c) select a hardware profile with
devices the guest has inbox drivers for; they are manual, offline guests
and their compatibility cells stay "not verified" until real evidence.

oneOf.description: Ubuntu LTS x86_64 (MVP reference guest).
Other Linux x86_64: manageable manually, without compatibility guarantees.
Windows XP (NT 5.1, and XP x64 / NT 5.2): legacy BIOS, i440fx, PIIX IDE.
Windows Vista (NT 6.0): legacy BIOS, q35, AHCI.
Windows 7 (NT 6.1): legacy BIOS, q35, AHCI.
Windows 8.1 (NT 6.3): UEFI (x64) or legacy BIOS (32-bit), q35, AHCI.

Windows 10 (NT 10.0, build < 22000): UEFI (x64) or legacy BIOS
(32-bit), q35, AHCI.

InputBatch.description:
Batch of input events tied to a run and a geometry: the core
rejects batches tied to a superseded `run_id` or a non-current geometry
(ROADMAP 6.4). Inputs are never repeated automatically.

ParentLossPolicy.description:
Fate of the VMs when the UI that started the service ends without a
controlled shutdown (crash, forced termination). ADR-0015 part B.

Orderly (ACPI) shutdown with a bounded wait, then `quit` and
termination; finally shutdown of the service.

Wait for the ACPI shutdown per VM, in seconds
([`MIN_PARENT_LOSS_POWERDOWN_S`]..=[`MAX_PARENT_LOSS_POWERDOWN_S`]).

PointerButton.description: Press or release of a pointer button.

Quotas.description:

Markdown view (texts escaped).
Liveness check.
Capabilities of the service and the backend.
List of the catalog VMs (UI only).
Status of a VM (UI only).
Creation of a VM in the catalog (UI only; never from agent sessions).

Change to the configuration of a stopped VM: resources and limits
(UI only; the disk can only grow).

expected_revision.description: Expected revision: a concurrent change is rejected.

oneOf.description:
Action on an existing VM through the core's queue (UI only in F1).
The response arrives after the backend outcome, except for `stop`
with a backend that stops in the background (QEMU): the response
arrives when the graceful stop has started (operation `forwarded`, VM
`stopping`) and the end is published as a `vm_state` event.
Subscription to state events (UI only).
List of active connections (UI only).
Revocation of a connection and its credential (UI only).
Issuing of a pairing credential to be delivered out of band (UI only).
Emergency Stop: priority path, does not go through the queue (UI only).

Fate of the VMs if the UI ends without a controlled shutdown (UI only).
Takes effect immediately; the UI sends it again at every service start.
Controlled shutdown of the service (UI only).
Approved media of the registry (UI only).

Import of an ISO chosen by the user with the native picker of the UI
(UI only, never from agent sessions): read-only managed copy, SHA-256
and registry row (ADR-0008). The path is opened as a regular file
without following links and is never passed to QEMU.

declared_origin.description: Origin declared by the user (free text, never interpreted).

oneOf.description: Deletion of a stopped VM with its disk and run files (UI only).

expected_revision.description: Expected revision: a concurrent change is rejected.

oneOf.description:
Console of a running VM (UI only): per-run display ticket (ADR-0013).
The ticket is revoked when the run ends, on Emergency Stop and when
the connection is revoked.
Baselines of a VM (UI only, F3).

Creation of a baseline with the VM off (UI only, F3; ROADMAP 8,
ADR-0005): the VM's current disk and UEFI variables are materialized
into a standalone, read-only, hashed baseline. Long operation (a
`qemu-img convert` of the whole disk): it runs outside the supervisor
thread, the VM is busy meanwhile (`vm_busy` for other mutations,
[`VmBaselines::operation`] set) and the reply arrives when it ends.
Cancelled by the Emergency Stop, by the revocation or closing of the
connection and by the service shutdown (nothing is published).

allow_unclean.description:
The last run did not end with an observed clean guest shutdown
(forced stop, Emergency Stop, crash, supervisor restart since):
without this flag the creation is refused (`state_conflict`,
detail `reason` = `unclean_shutdown`); with it the baseline is
recorded as **not verified** (`clean_shutdown: false`) and is
never promoted to verified later.

oneOf.description:
Restore of a baseline with the VM off (UI only, F3): the VM's current
state (standalone disk or previous overlay, and UEFI variables) is
**discarded** and replaced by a new QCOW2 overlay backed by the
baseline plus a fresh copy of the baseline's UEFI variables. The
baseline's hash is verified first. The guest restarts with a normal
boot at the next start. The reply arrives when done, as for
`create_baseline` (same cancellation rules).

Deletion of a baseline (UI only, F3; the UI asks for confirmation).
Refused if the baseline is in use (the VM's current state is an
overlay of it) or protected.

Session request of an agent (`pairing` role only, F4): refused while
the agent access switch is off. The reply carries the verification
code the user compares in the app; the decision is awaited with
[`Request::AwaitSession`].

client_name.description:
Client name declared by the agent (free text, at most
[`MAX_CLIENT_NAME_CHARS`] characters kept, never interpreted).

purpose.description:
Purpose declared by the agent (free text, at most
[`MAX_PURPOSE_CHARS`] characters kept, never interpreted).

requested_capabilities.description: Capabilities the agent would like (a hint for the user).

requested_vms.description: VMs the agent would like (a hint for the user).

oneOf.description:
Waits for the user's decision on a session request of this
connection (`pairing` role only). Long: the reply arrives when the
user approves or denies, or when the request expires.

Call of an agent session bound to this connection (`pairing` role
only). Checked by the core on receipt and right before forwarding.
State of the agent access switch (UI only).

Agent access switch (UI only): off at every service start. Turning it
off denies the pending requests and revokes the live sessions.
Pending session requests (UI only).
Approval of a session request (UI only).
Denial of a session request (UI only).
Agent sessions, live first (UI only).
Agent pause (UI only): agent mutations refused, the VM keeps running.
Resume after a pause (UI only).

Revocation (UI only): the session ends, its queue is discarded, the
agent connection is closed; the VM is not stopped.

Input ownership of a VM (UI only): take control back or hand it to an
agent session. Pressed keys and buttons are released on every change.

Session reports, newest first (UI only, F5). Reports survive service
restarts; sessions do not.
Header of a report, without events (UI only).
A page of the events of a report (UI only).
Chunk of a stored screenshot of a report (UI only).

Explicit judgement of the local user on a session (UI only): sets the
outcome with the rationale, attributed to the user.
Runs an automatic verifier on the session's evidence (UI only).

Export of a report to a file chosen by the user with the native save
dialog (UI only; MCP can never choose a destination).

destination.description: Absolute path of the new file.

include_screenshots.description: Also write the stored screenshots next to the file.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file (the user confirmed it).

RunId.description: RunId: version 7 UUID, lowercase with hyphens.

Duration of the grant in seconds
([`MIN_SESSION_DURATION_S`]..=[`MAX_SESSION_DURATION_S`]).

give_input.description: Hand input control of the VM to the agent at once.

vm_id.description: The single VM of the session (MVP).

SessionAuth.description:
Credential of an agent session, carried by every [`Request::Agent`].
`Debug` redacts the token.

SessionId.description: SessionId: version 7 UUID, lowercase with hyphens.

SessionToken.description: Session secret, only on authenticated IPC; never in logs or reports.

SessionVerifier.description: Automatic verifier the user can run on a session.

oneOf.description: ADR-0019 pixel verifier on the last screenshot of the session.

TestOutcome.description:
Outcome of a test (ROADMAP 9). Completing the conversation does not
automatically produce `passed`.

oneOf.description: Criteria verified.
Criteria not met.
No reliable verifier or insufficient evidence.
Cancelled by the user.
Time ran out.
Infrastructure failure, distinct from a model failure.

VmAction.description: Action requested on an existing VM.

oneOf.description: Start.
Ordinary stop.
Forced stop with OS primitives.
Guest reset.
Screenshot.
Typed input.

VmConfig.description:
VM configuration requested by the user. No field is a path or
a QEMU option: media are referenced by [`MediaId`] of the approved registry.

data_media.description: Optional read-only data media (kind `data_iso`), attached with the VM off.

disk_gib.description: Virtual size of the main QCOW2 disk in GiB.

install_media.description: Installation media from the media registry (kind `install_iso`).

limits.description:
Execution limits applied by the supervisor to the QEMU process
(ADR-0017); missing in older catalogs → default values.

memory_mib.description: Guest memory in MiB (not the limit of the whole QEMU process).

network.description: Network profile; in the MVP only `offline`.

vcpus.description: Number of vCPUs (not a CPU percentage limit: ROADMAP 7.2).

VmId.description: VmId: version 7 UUID, lowercase with hyphens.

VmLimits.description:
Execution limits of a VM (ADR-0017), set by the user in the
VM settings and applied by the supervisor, never by the client.

cpu_max_percent.description:
CPU cap as a percentage of the capacity of the assigned vCPUs
([`MIN_CPU_MAX_PERCENT`]..=100; 100 = no cap). Applied by the
operating system to the whole QEMU process.

memory_margin_mib.description:
Memory granted to the QEMU process beyond the guest RAM, in MiB
([`MIN_MEMORY_MARGIN_MIB`]..=[`MAX_MEMORY_MARGIN_MIB`]). When the
limit is exceeded, QEMU is terminated and the exit is classified as a resource limit.

storage_budget_gib.description:
Maximum space in GiB for the VM's files beyond the main disk
(overlays, baselines, firmware variables); `None` = no dedicated budget.
Checked at every start.

VmName.description: VM name: ASCII label, not a path.

VmRequest.description: Request for an action on a VM.

expected_run_id.description:
Expected run: mandatory for reset, screenshot and input; if present
and different from the current run the request is rejected (`state_conflict`).

operation_id.description:
Idempotency key chosen by the caller: the same request repeated with
the same `operation_id` does not duplicate the effect.
